title: Sauce de foleré au poisson fumé (Roselle Leaf Sauce with Smoked Fish)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Boiled and drained foleré leaves added to fried onion, smoked fish, tomatoes and spices, then water, roasted peanut paste, salt, pepper and natron, cooked 15–20 minutes.
longDesc: p. 58 of the October 2023 recipe book. Fresh foleré leaves are boiled and drained. Onion is fried; the fish, tomatoes, garlic, green condiments and spices are simmered in; the leaves go in; then water, roasted peanut paste, salt, pepper and natron, and the sauce cooks 15–20 minutes. The book’s cue: natron reduces the acidity of the foleré. No quantities are printed.
ingredients: Fresh foleré leaves — quantity not printed
Roasted peanut paste — quantity not printed
Water, oil, onion, garlic, tomatoes, bell pepper, leek, parsley, celery, white pepper, ginger, salt, chilli — quantities not printed
steps: Boil the foleré leaves and drain them.
Fry the onion. Add the fish, tomatoes, garlic, green condiments and spices and simmer.
Add water, the peanut paste, salt, pepper and natron.
chefTips: The printed reason for the natron is to reduce the acidity of the foleré.
No other doneness cue is printed.
commonMistakes: Adding the peanut paste without water.
healthBenefits: Foleré (roselle) leaves are a leafy green; smoked fish and peanuts add protein.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Sauce de foleré au poisson fumé’ (p. 58).
